body:
# Independent audit of the integer-fiber affine contact certificate

Read `candidate 18f8d2b72265ccb5`
in full. Result: **PASS**, with no mathematical correction required.

The positive base set is lattice-convex, and the compatible source hull
has exactly the retained positive fibers. Source-only affine fits can
therefore be realized inside C, with exact one-sided thickening when
the base hull has deficient rank. For q=d, every fiber volume scales by
the same det(T), the true base centroid stays integer, and normalized
depth is preserved by the ambient affine bijection. This justifies
determinant maximality using only integer-fiber constraints.

The constraint family and its zero-slack contact subset are compact.
A parameter direction strictly decreasing every active constraint and
strictly increasing trace is uniformly feasible for a small step:
near-contact gradients have a common negative margin, and the remaining
constraints have positive minimum slack. The determinant derivative at
identity is trace, so that direction is impossible. Strict separation
then gives the stated finite Fritz--John alternative. The signs, matrix
transposes and p+1 contact bound agree with the parameter pairing;
when alpha>0, conic Caratheodory gives p contact terms.

A strict integer-fiber fit pairs negatively with every contact gradient
and rules out the pure abnormal alternative. No positive determinant is
needed for that auxiliary strict fit, since a short segment from identity
remains orientation preserving. With polytopal source and target fibers,
the feasible fitting system is finite linear. Global determinant
maximality forces trace to be maximized at identity over this whole
polyhedron, and ordinary LP duality supplies the normal certificate
without a Slater assumption.

Translation and base-shear balances cancel exactly in
`sum lambda u(x-Qz-c_0)^T`; tracing yields alpha*d and the support-value
identity. They do not cancel independently chosen integer cap normals.
No contact weights are silently identified with cap or section masses.

The eight-corner height example is centrally symmetric in the full
ambient space, so D=C is an actual global extraction maximum at local
half-depth. Its necessary corner interval inequalities exclude every
strict affine fit after averaging against z_1*z_2*z_3. Nevertheless one
corner's two endpoint contacts give the claimed normalized stress.

Finally the sqrt(z) example has only one ambient contact, with continuous
normal zero. Its small-z width ratio forces ambient |T|<=1, while its
single positive integer fiber can be doubled inside C. Thus it correctly
refutes an ambient-fit normality argument and does not purport to be a
globally maximal extracted source.

The general abnormal alternative and the absence of a retained-mass
fraction are appropriately preserved throughout.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
